Factory Life is a first-person factory simulator with colony-management elements. Betrayed by the ideals you believed in: hard work and sacrifice. What did it bring you? Now you must find your own path. Will you be able to change anything, or will you become the very thing you hate? 

Grow Big

Start at the very bottom, working alone in a grimy garage. Gather people like you to build something greater together. Take care of their needs, manage their schedule, and avoid burning them out. Or be a tyrant. Forge your own path.

Create

Put your hands back to work. Assemble electronics on your own, earn money, buy materials, and acquire new licenses. Satisfy your clients and offer increasingly better products. Show them that you are someone to be reckoned with.

A Whole Pipeline

Assemble, inspect, and pack electronics. Build assembly lines made of human hands. Optimize your workflow and cut costs to stay competitive as demands continue to rise. Are you up for the challenge?

Strong Like a Tree

Expand your skills and watch your potential grow. Over time you will become stronger, mastering more complex tasks. Just remember that with great power comes great responsibility.

To the Top

Compete. Produce more, better, and faster than others. Build a stronger position as you race up the leaderboard against other manufacturers. Don't give up, and you will eventually reach the top. But will it be worth it?

Key Features:

  • Start from Scratch: Be a one-man assembly line and build everything with your own hands.

  • Automate: Hire workers to boost your production and scale your operations.

  • Manage: Optimize workflow, take care of your crew's needs, and make tough choices.

  • Unique Setting: Experience the harsh reality of 1980s Asia.

  • Good or Evil: Decide what kind of boss you want to be.

  • Reach the Top: Outperform the competition and prove you are the best.

Connect, Produce, Sell, and Expand


Factory New Idle is a relaxing automation and idle game where you build your factory from interconnected nodes.

Begin with natural resources such as water sources, forests, and mines. Connect their raw materials to pumps, purifiers, workshops, furnaces, and other production facilities. Every new connection expands your factory, while increasingly advanced production lines create more valuable goods.

Build Your Own Production Network


Every node has its own inputs, outputs, and connection points. Control the flow of resources, link facilities together, and transform raw materials into finished products one step at a time.

Produce clean water, turn wood into furniture, process minerals, build fishing chains, and discover many more production paths. How your factory is arranged—and how efficiently everything flows—is entirely up to you.

Purchase New Nodes


Spend your profits on new resource sources, machines, production facilities, and markets. Every node offers another way to expand your existing factory or begin a completely new production chain.

Match the right machines with the right resources, balance their inputs, and eliminate the bottlenecks slowing down your network.

Expand the Skill Tree


Earn skill points through production and progress through specialized water, wood, ore, and other technology branches. Unlock new facilities, advanced machines, and increasingly profitable products.

Every unlock gives you more options to make your factory faster, more efficient, and more valuable.

Optimize Your Production


Upgrade nodes to improve their production speed and capacity. Reroute connections, manage resource distribution, and make sure every part of the factory receives the inputs it needs.

Transform a simple resource line into a massive interconnected network capable of producing many different goods at once.

Sell Your Products and Keep Growing


Connect resources and finished products to markets, sell everything your factory creates, and reinvest the profits. Purchase more nodes, unlock new technologies, and construct larger, more complex production lines.

In Factory New Idle, every connection creates a new opportunity—and every upgrade brings your growing factory one step closer to perfect automation.

  • Freely place and connect production nodes
  • Build water, wood, ore, fishing, and many other production chains
  • Purchase and upgrade resources, machines, and facilities
  • Progress through specialized skill-tree branches
  • Manage inputs, outputs, capacity, and production times
  • Automate complete production lines from natural resources to finished goods
  • Enjoy a steadily growing idle economy with satisfying progression

In the darkness, breathing is your only control.

Fading Edge is a side-scrolling adventure controlled by your breath. Inhale to slow your steps; exhale to run faster — but every breath awakens nightmares deeper below.

▎Breath Is Life and Death
Every inhale and exhale directly affects your movement speed. Pressure builds in the dark — when it peaks, nightmares will tear through your last three drops of blood.

▎Nightmares Show No Mercy
Stationary ones, stalkers, hunters, red ones — they are not level decoration, but hunters that think. Some dodge your gaze, some predict your path, some cannot be dispelled at all.

▎Echoes Are the Only Salvation
Echo shards lie scattered across the abyss. Touch them — pressure resets, nightmares dissolve. But peace never lasts. Deeper down, more await.

▎Four Abysses, Four Kinds of Forgetting
Forgetting (black and white), Obsession (cold blue), Letting Go (warm white), Origin (warm gold) — every abyss is a ruin of memory. The deeper you go, the lonelier it becomes.

▎A Dream Within a Dream
Sometimes a swirling black hole appears in the dark. Step inside — another world awaits. Piece together the shards, reclaim the memories stolen from you... or be trapped in the dream forever.

· High-contrast black-and-white hand-drawn style with rough brushstrokes
· Unique breath-based controls at the core
· Three drops of blood — death means starting over. Respect the dark.
· Fragmented storytelling — a treasure for collectors on a second playthrough

Stop breathing... and you die.

You're not trapped. You're just misplaced.

 

Infinite hallways? Yes. Something lurking in the dark? Probably. A bathroom designed for two people to use at the same time? Unfortunately, yes.

 

Welcome to FailRooms, a strange world of liminal spaces inspired by the Backrooms, where fear of the unknown meets terrible architecture. Expect stairs that lead into ceilings, bone-dry pools, fake doors, and rooms that make absolutely no sense.

Explore a place where nothing feels right

 Wander through endless spaces built in ways they never should have been. The deeper you go, the harder it becomes to tell whether something is dangerous... or just another terrible design choice.

 

Laugh at the absurd... while you still can

 One moment, you're alone in a silent hallway. The next, you're staring at something so badly designed that you forget you're supposed to be scared. FailRooms turns liminal horror into something stranger, funnier, and much less predictable.

 

Don't let your guard down

 Feeling comfortable is usually a bad sign. Empty hallways aren't always empty, harmless-looking things may not stay harmless, and some mistakes are more dangerous than others.

 Keep moving, stay alert, and whatever you do, stay away from the rubber duck.

 

Will you find a way out, or will FailRooms keep you lost inside?

Free pixel-art blackjack. The goal is simple: get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over.

Three ways to play

  • Solo table: no waiting, start a hand anytime.
  • Three-seat table: share a table with other players; empty seats fill automatically.
  • Seven-hand elimination: three players, the lowest stack is out after hand 4, and the biggest stack after hand 7 wins.

Easy to pick up

  • Beginner hints: on your turn, the best move by standard strategy lights up. Prefer to decide yourself? Turn it off in Settings.
  • Full rules: hit, stand, double, split, insurance and surrender. Natural blackjack pays 3:2, dealer stands on soft 17.
  • Chips every day: check in daily for growing rewards, and if you run out, claim a refill up to 3 times a day.
  • 20 Steam achievements.

Actually fair

Before every deal the server locks in a cryptographic commitment; after settlement the full card order and every action are revealed. Open any finished hand in the verifier, replay it, and check the result yourself.

Also

  • Friend rooms: share an invite code and sit at the same table.
  • Weekly leaderboard.
  • Swap pixel tables, card backs, avatars and music anytime.

KEY FEATURES

High-Octane Combat

Experience pure action satisfaction through seamless skill casting, split-second dodge dashes, fluid combo chaining, and screen-clearing spell synergies.

Limitless Build Diversity, Legendary Weapons & Runes

Transcend simple stat boosts. Equip Class-Specific Legendary Weapons and Unique Armors that fundamentally alter how your abilities function. Inscribe your gear with Void Runes to trigger devastating secondary detonations on impact, lock your most vital affix at the Enchanter to forge the perfect item, and tailor distinct combat archetypes across the Ascension Tree.

Brutal Boss Encounters

Awaken ancient guardians and stand against towering Void colossi that push your reflexes, positioning, and build efficiency to their absolute limits.

Adapt and Master Your Playstyle

Completely reshape your setup. Master a roster of classes, each driven by distinct resource management mechanics, dedicated passive loops, and signature skills. Endure escalating trial arenas and claim your place on the Leaderboards.

WHEN THE VOID SHATTERS REALITY, YOU ARE THE LAST SHIELD.

As a cosmic cataclysm strikes the continent of Voidreach, warping the very fabric of reality, the once-sacred Shattered Saint Astra awakens anew at the core of darkness. You are an awakened champion thrust into an unforgiving world—stretching from the besieged ramparts of Bastion of Hope and the toxic roots of Whispering Grove, to the fanatical cults of Ruined Coast and the frozen chasms of Barren Peaks.

Will you purge the corruption at its roots, or bend the overwhelming might of the Void into your own weapon?

FallChess: Wizard's Chess

Traditional chess. First-person duels. The piece doesn't move on its own — you do.

Inspired by the iconic wizard's chess duel, FallChess: Wizard's Chess brings chess into a fully 3D world. Choose your character, mount your piece, move across the board, and face your opponent up close.

The rules remain faithful to classic chess. Pawns, Knights, Bishops, Rooks, Queens, and Kings move just as you know them. The difference is that now, you are the one riding the piece.

FEATURES

♟️ Classic chess, a new perspective
Play with the familiar rules of chess, including castling, promotion, and draw by repetition, on a fully 3D board.

🧙 Choose your character
Play as Aiko, Hanna, Ravi, or Sabrina — each with their own color and visual identity on the board.

🐴 Mount, move, capture
Directly control the piece you're mounted on. Choose who rides each piece before the match begins — once the first move is made, those choices are locked in.

🌐 Multiplayer
Play PvP or PvE, locally or online, with up to 2 players per team or 4 players in co-op.

⏱️ Configurable clock
Choose the pace of your match, from Bullet to Classic.

🎥 Dynamic cameras
Switch between board view, free orbit, and third-person perspectives. If your character is eliminated, take control of a free-fly camera and keep watching the battle.

🌍 Multi-language
Localized interface with dedicated font support for Japanese, Korean, Russian, Chinese, Hindi, and Arabic.

ABOUT THE GAME

FallChess: Wizard's Chess was created to give chess a body — literally.

Instead of simply watching pieces move across a board, you step into the game. Choose your character, mount your piece, and experience every move from within the match. Every capture puts you face to face with your opponent.

Board strategy meets first-person action.

Chess like it's never been played before.

A Fictional Cultivation World – The Nine Provinces

The game begins in a self-evolving cultivation world. You start as a mortal or a rogue cultivator and rise through multiple paths. As you travel across different regions, you advance your cultivation realm, gather techniques, magical treasures, and spirit pets, and befriend rogue cultivators or members of various factions. If you become powerful enough, your choices will influence the direction of the world.

Free and Open Paths to Cultivation

The game offers many ways to grow stronger: alchemy, artifact forging, merchant trading, killing for loot, rogue trading, body refining, demonic cultivation, and more. You can choose the methods you are good at and enjoy, then put your skills to the test against challengers at the same realm.

Faction Conflicts and Strategic Intrigue

As you travel through the Nine Provinces, you will meet key figures of this world, learn about its past and present, observe their calculations and ambitions, and interact with them. At each stage of your cultivation, your choices determine what you gain – and who will walk alongside you as fellow Daoists.

Semi-Real-Time Combat with Multiple Schools

Inspired by the magic duels in cultivation anime, the combat system features diverse schools: Five Elements, Overwhelming Force, Body Refining, Treasure Master, Beast Taming, and more. The other cultivators you face may also be masters of these schools – to defeat them, you must find the right approach from many possibilities.

Combat is presented in 3D, blending strategic turn-based planning with real-time action. You experience the thrill of live combat, yet you can pause at any moment to rethink and adjust your tactics.

Fallen Nights combines top-down zombie survival with tower defense. Scavenge by day, build your defenses and fight beside them when the horde closes in. Every piece of scrap spent protecting your camp is a piece you could have used to repair your escape.

The zombies are coming for that escape, too. Hold the approaches, deal with enemies that slip through and decide how much longer you can afford to stay. Your defenses help hold the line, but you are still out there with a weapon in your hands.

Daylight is your chance to prepare. Explore the surrounding area, strip abandoned cars and gather scrap before the next attack. Bring it back to strengthen the camp, replace a lost defense or put more parts into your escape.

Each trip leaves you with another choice: invest in a stronger position for the next night, or push the repairs closer to completion? When your preparations are done, call the night early and put your setup to the test.

Build at marked sites around your camp and choose what each position needs. A site covering a busy approach might earn its keep with a turret, while a mine can punish enemies that bunch together.

  • Turrets add steady fire while you fight nearby.

  • Mines deliver an explosive hit against a crowd.

  • Barricades and spikes help hold up enemies and buy you room to react.

Upgrade and repair your defenses as the run develops. Placement is simple, but spending everything on the camp means leaving less scrap for your escape.

Choose upgrade cards as you level up and shape the weapons you bring into each fight. Build around rifle fire, the close-range punch of a shotgun or a fast-firing SMG, then add grenades, rockets or Molotovs to handle a crowded approach.

Experiment with combinations and discover synergies that make your chosen weapons stronger. Your equipment and defenses work together: cover a lane with a turret while you deal with another threat, or use an explosive when enemies gather. Watch your footing around your own fire, because it can hurt you too.

The full game takes you beyond the demo's Riverside into new locations, from wooded roads to snowy mountain terrain and a fortified bunker. Each location brings different approaches to defend and an escape to work toward.

Carry the same hard choice into each new location: how much do you spend surviving here, and how much do you put toward getting out?

Try six survivors with different strengths, choose another set of upgrades and rethink which defenses deserve your scrap. A different weapon combination gives you another reason to return to a familiar map.

For another challenge, take on Endless mode or the Daily Run. Simple controls and marked build sites keep the focus on the decisions you make during the action: where to stand, what to build and when to make your escape.

Turn the world around you and use gravity to reach your goal. Run through concrete structures where there is no up or down. Collect strange orbs. Experience the contrast between the city and nature. Avoid the monstrous spider Karl, who is watching to make sure your desire for freedom turns into a free fall.

Heroes want glory. You have bills to pay.

Fame & Fear: Dungeon Architect is a single-player fantasy management sandbox. Build a dungeon full of monsters, traps and treasure, open inns and attract adventurers willing to pay to get in.

Admission is paid up front. Getting home isn't included.

Build a dungeon worth the risk

Dig out rooms and corridors, place doors, and choose floors, lighting and decorations. Mix and match different themes, place your monsters and give your bosses a spot worthy of their worst intentions.

Layout matters: treasure can draw visitors down a particular route, and a trap can help a monster land its attacks. Filling a room with danger won't do much good if nobody sets foot in it.

Plan at night. Face the consequences by day.

Prepare your dungeon at night and use the Predicted Flow Heatmap to spot promising routes and areas that might stay empty. It's a forecast, not a promise: adventurers have needs and plans of their own. Select them during a visit to see where they're going and why.

When things need a little nudge, use your Keeper's Orders. Use Lure to make an area more appealing; Overcharge to boost a trap's next activation at the cost of a longer cooldown; and Seal to temporarily close a passage without cutting off essential escape routes. You have three uses in total per day. Blowing all three on the first curious visitor is an option. Not necessarily a good one.

At the end of the day, check the report: damage, object usage, revenue and observations based on what actually happened. Then get back to building. Maybe that trap was a great idea, just in the wrong corridor.

An inn between two traps is still an inn

Set your admission price, furnish the rooms, hire staff and offer services to your visitors. Basic furniture and staff are available from Rank F; beds and guest rooms unlock at Rank C. You can use furniture from different themes without sticking to a single matching set.

Keep an eye on expenses, maintenance and your cash reserves: an overpriced ticket can turn people away, and those who do enter might want to spend some money at the inn too. Some adventurers come back, bringing memories of their last visit with them.

It's good to have a regular customer. Especially one you've already tried to kill.

Someone has to make it out alive

A dungeon without danger doesn't give visitors much of a story to tell. One without survivors has a different problem: nobody left to tell it.

Balance fame, fear and survival to keep adventurers coming. Over time, your dungeon's lethality, trap usage and the success of your services can influence how well prepared incoming groups are, who's in them and how much money they bring.

And then there's the Kingdom. Let fear get out of hand and you might receive an official visit. The kind with weapons, not clipboards.

From Rank F to Legendary Dungeon

Grow your dungeon from Rank F all the way to SS, tackle objectives and see what new content awaits before paying for a promotion.

At Rank SS, you can take on the Kingdom's Grand Expedition, an optional challenge with three days to prepare. Complete it to earn the title of Legendary Dungeon.

There's no mandatory finale: the sandbox continues, whether you take on the challenge or not. There's always another room to sort out.

Good ideas deserve a blueprint

Save your rooms as blueprints, reuse them in other playthroughs and share them through the Steam Workshop.

Designed a particularly unpleasant welcome? It would be a shame to keep it to yourself.

FARM · BUILD · SHOOT · DEFEND · TOGETHER

Farm by day and fight side by side at night! Fancy Farm Brawl blends farming, tower-defense strategy, and fast top-down shooting. Grow crops, earn coins, strengthen your home, then grab your weapons and face swarms of monsters and formidable bosses.


Team Up in Two-Player Attack & Defense

Fight alongside a partner in two-player Attack & Defense mode. Hold the line together, split your roles, cover each other when the pressure rises, and keep your farm standing against increasingly fierce assaults.

Fast Shooting Meets Tower Defense

Move freely, swap attacks to match the situation, unleash powerful special moves, and build a defensive position. Read enemy routes and attack patterns, then balance raw firepower with smart defense to control the battlefield.


Build a Farm Worth Fighting For

Plant and harvest crops, explore colorful corners of Qilin Island, and invest your hard-earned resources in your farm and home. Every day of farming helps prepare you for the next battle.



Varied Battlefields and Memorable Bosses

Cross obstacle-filled courses, tackle defense and pursuit objectives in distinctive regions, and confront dangerous bosses—including the mighty Ape King. Learn their attack patterns, find your opening, and turn the fight around.



Key Features

  • A distinctive mix of farming, tower defense, and top-down action shooting
  • Cooperate with a partner in two-player Attack & Defense mode
  • Build your defenses, dodge enemy attacks, and unleash powerful special moves
  • Explore varied regions and face monster swarms and memorable bosses
  • Meet the quirky residents of Qilin Island

Play the Free Demo — Wishlist Now!

Download the free Demo and experience farming, shooting, and frantic farm defense for yourself. If Qilin Island feels like your kind of adventure, add Fancy Farm Brawl to your wishlist and follow its journey toward launch!

The voxel world has shattered, its altars broken and its order lost. You wake beneath a great tree as an adventurer meant to put it back together: pick your race and class, head into a world that is different every time, and find the lost altars.

Terrain, biomes and encounters are recombined every time, so there is no fixed route. Forests, snowfields, deserts, grasslands and islands each have their own look, and day, night and the seasons keep turning. More than ten kinds of wonders, from a colossal tree to frozen falls and a whale-bone harbor, wait to be found, and gliders, boats and a grappling hook carry you over mountains and seas.

Every village has its own people and trades. The blacksmith upgrades and modifies your weapons, the stable looks after your pets and hatches eggs, the warehouse keeps your loot safe, and someone in the tavern always wants a word. Spend time with the villagers and their friendship grows; after dark, the village needs you to help its guards hold the line.

Human, Elf, Orc and Undead each bring their own talents, and the four classes play completely differently: the Warrior charges in behind a shield, the Mage commands the elements, the Ranger shoots from afar and the Ninja strikes from behind.

  • A skill tree with three paths and freely spent points

  • Pick one talent per tier, so the same class can grow into different styles

  • Passives and a star map to fine-tune your build

  • Advance into a stronger class once you are ready, or change class and start fresh

Dodge-roll, raise your shield, time a parry. The last hit of a combo sweeps the whole pack, and a wounded foe can be finished in a single execute. Every enemy attack is telegraphed, so if you read it you walk away clean.

Each main boss has its own arena and a full moveset. Once one falls, you decide its fate, and each choice brings different rewards and consequences. More than twenty kinds of regional bosses are scattered across the world, waiting for a challenger.

Hundreds of pieces of gear, each with its own look. Complete a set to unlock its set bonus, and random affixes make the same item play differently. The blacksmith can upgrade and modify your gear, and you can dye or transmog the looks you love.

Twenty-four creatures can become your companions: tame them in the wild, or bring an egg back to the stable and hatch it. Companions fight at your side and use their own skills; once your bond is strong enough you can ride them, and some will carry you into the sky.

Explore at your own pace alone, or invite friends through Steam and adventure together with up to 8 players, bosses included.

Fangjie: Shattered Altars is in Early Access. At launch you can play all four races, four classes, the full world and its villages, several main bosses, regional bosses, pets and mounts, and online co-op. Throughout Early Access I will keep shipping major updates with more content and balance changes, and every one of them is free for everyone who owns the game.

They stole your soul. Now take it back.

Far Away Kingdom is a fast-paced arcade gallery shooter inspired by classics like Wild Guns, Cabal and Blood Bros.
Aim, dodge and fight your way through relentless enemy waves, dense bullet patterns and massive bosses in a world determined to stop you.

Choose your path, master your character and turn every run into a fight for survival — and revenge.

Switch between Fire and Ice, unleash devastating special weapons, and learn when to move, dash or stand your ground. Every encounter is built around precision, positioning and quick reactions.

Play solo or join forces in local co-op, where both players share the same battlefield, the same dangers — and the same limited chances to survive.

FEATURES

• Fast, skill-based arcade combat inspired by classic gallery shooters

• Fire and Ice mechanics that change how you approach enemies and encounters

• Special weapons including Lightning, Homing Shots, Triple Shot and Black Holes

• Dense enemy patterns designed around movement, positioning and precision

• Large boss battles with unique attack patterns and mechanics

• Local 2-player co-op

• Multiple paths with alternate stages throughout the campaign

• Secret levels, hidden bosses and collectibles

• Rank-based progression rewarding accuracy, speed and performance

• Multiple endings — uncover every secret to reach the true conclusion

• Controller and keyboard + mouse support, with optional twin-stick aiming

Fight harder. Aim better. Find what they hid from you.

Your revenge is only the beginning.

Face relentless enemies, improve your skills, and push your limits in a classic arcade experience with modern mechanics.

You wake up on a strange planet with a Gatling Gun in one hand and a debt notice in the other.

Your name is Eira. You owe $100,000 to an interstellar bank that does not negotiate.

To survive, you'll need to raise living ammunition, hunt alien creatures, haul your loot home by the kilogram, and make payments on time - or face what comes after.

YOUR BULLETS ARE ALIVE

Hatch living ammo in the Bio-Lab by combining eggs with food. Three ammo types, three combat identities:

  • Bran - Rapid-fire crowd control. Creates miniature black holes.

  • Protein - Armor-piercing devastation. Punches through multiple enemies.

  • Spinach - Smart explosives that deploy homing chicks to hunt down survivors.

Max your skills to unlock Cross Mutations, devastating hybrid abilities born from mastered combos.

LOOT HAS WEIGHT

No slots, no Tetris - everything is kilograms. Stuff your bag, and you'll slow down. Fill it completely, and you can't move at all. Rare loot is heavier. Every prize is a gamble between greed and survival.

THE BANK ALWAYS COLLECTS

Miss a payment and your debt grows 5% every 10 seconds. Stay overdue long enough, and the bank sends a Debt Collector Boss to settle things personally. Kill the Collector? Your debt increases, and the next one arrives stronger.

Or pay off everything and face the real question: walk away free, or sign a new loan for $10 billion.

RISK EVERYTHING. OPEN THE POD.

Mysterious Supply Pods crash-land in 4 tiers of escalating danger. Open one with the wrong ammo type and you'll trigger 1 of 14 Curses - from gun jamming and locked shops to instant debt collector summons.

Build Your Survival Strategy

Upgrade your skills, optimize your economy, and evolve your ammo to survive longer against both monsters and capitalism.

FEATURES

  • Hatch living ammunition from eggs and food in the Bio-Lab

  • 3 unique ammo types with distinct combat behaviors and evolution paths

  • Charge shots, recoil-jump, and weaponize gun overheats

  • Physics-based weight inventory - no slots, just kilograms

  • 5-tier rarity system: Stardust > Nebula > Quasar > Supernova > Singularity

  • 4-tier Supply Pods with 14 unique curses

  • Predatory debt system with escalating collectors, compound penalties, and early settlement options

  • Dynamic economy: sales tax, inflation, and a black market endgame

  • 3-branch skill tree with milestone power spikes and Cross Mutation synergies

  • Day/night cycle with midnight Night Events

  • Enemies with ammo resistance and elite mutations (Juggernaut, Assassin, Berserker)

  • Multi-phase bosses with laser sweeps, bomb rain, vortexes, and more

  • Achievement trophy cabinet

  • Multi-map world with fast travel waystones

  • Lua modding API with in-game developer terminal

  • Robust save system with 3-layer backup protection

  • "In Media Res" tutorial - 60 seconds of invincible chaos, then the debt collector arrives

Across the dry lands of rural Africa, many people and organizations came with temporary aid.

Food was delivered.
Supplies were handed out.
Then everything slowly disappeared again.

But But you are here to do something different. You are here to bring lasting life, civilization, and self-sufficiency.

Inspired by the real humanitarian journey of Quang Linh and his African volunteer team, Farm Of Hope is a cozy farming and community-building simulation about helping a village grow through hard work, kindness, and sustainable farming.

You are not here to save the world overnight.

You are here to plant the first seeds of hope.

🌱 TURN DRY LAND INTO A THRIVING COMMUNITY

Start your journey in a small village surrounded by drought, poor soil, and empty water tanks.

Together with the local community, you will slowly transform the land through farming, irrigation, education, and cooperation.

Plant crops.
Raise animals.
Dig wells.
Build a future.

Watch the environment evolve from dry dust into vibrant green life.

  • Grow corn, cassava, pineapple, rice, and vegetables

  • Build irrigation systems and water wells

She was the only one who could read it. Now she's dead, and it's still running.

A rune-tape program runs the pressure ward that keeps the Drifted City aloft. It ran correctly for eleven years. Last night it killed the engineer who maintained it.

You have her listing. Her logs. Her stepper.

Find the instruction that did it.

You never write a line of code. You read one.

Faultfinder is a deduction game with a debugger for a magnifying glass. Every case opens as three panes: her annotated listing on the left, the machine's live state in the middle, and on the right what the city actually observed. A pressure reading that held at zero for nine seconds. A door that reported closed while it stood open.

Your tools are a debugger's, not a programmer's:

  • Step one instruction and watch exactly one thing change.

  • Break on a line, or on a condition: stop when PRESSURE drops below four.

  • Watch a register and read its whole history as a strip beside the tape.

  • Rewind. The entire trace is recorded. The scrub bar runs both ways.

  • Inject a different reading from the outside world and re-run it. Some faults only wake for one input in a thousand.

Then you commit. Name one line. Name one fault from a fixed vocabulary: off-by-one boundary, uninitialised register, wrong branch polarity, overwritten value, unit mismatch, missing bounds check. Then name the moment the harm was done. Get all three right and the report writes itself, one clause at a time.

Every case has exactly one answer. That is not a promise. It is a proof.

Faultfinder's cases aren't designed and playtested into fairness. They're machine-verified before they ship. Each one is built by taking a correct program, applying a single seeded fault, and then proving by exhaustive simulation across the whole input space that the faulty program fails, that reverting that one instruction fixes it, and that no other single change can.

If a case has a second defensible answer, the pipeline rejects it and you never see it. No designer ever adjudicates whether your reasoning was fair. The machine already did.

The program is a character document.

M. VOSK kept this ward for eleven years. She annotated her own tape in pencil, translating each rune for herself in her first year, because nobody had taught her either.

Her glosses thin as the cases go on. Her comments get terser. There is a line she commented out, years ago, with the note leave this.

You are the first person in eleven years to read her carefully. You are eleven years late.

For the specific pleasure almost no game has dramatised

If you have ever written software, you know the feeling of a bug collapsing into obviousness. The moment a mess becomes a sentence. Faultfinder makes that collapse the win condition and puts a body underneath it.

And if you haven't: you don't need to. Nothing here asks you to author anything. The blank page is the wall that keeps most players out of programming games, and this game does not have one. Her handwritten gloss sits beside every rune in the first case. Hover translates anything, always. No case is ever gated on remembering.

In the demo

  • Seven cases, 35 to 70 minutes, on one machine: the pressure ward on the city's underside

  • A fourteen-instruction rune-tape, taught by using it

  • Six classes of fault, each hiding in a different way

  • Full rewind, conditional breakpoints, register watches and input injection

  • Her story, told entirely in marginalia and log fragments

In most roguelites, power comes out of a chest. In FERAL PRINCE, it comes out of an enemy that is still moving.
Break its Soul Barrier, weaken it, and decide whether the battlefield is safe enough to extract a Soul Orb. Success leaves behind a weakened Husk intent on escape. The enemy you choose not to kill is the build you choose to make.

REVEAL EIGHT. LOCK FIVE.

At the end of the room, choose which extracted Orbs to forge into black-jade Soul Tiles. Each bears a rank, one of four suits, and an Engraving stolen from its source.
Reveal eight tiles from your bag and lock five for the next room. You get one partial redraw; once combat begins, the hand is sealed. No drawing, discarding, or build menu interrupts the fight.

YOUR HAND IS A FIGHTING STYLE

Your best five-tile poker hand grants a room-long combat effect and one charged Hand Skill. A Pair drills through one target twice. A Straight cuts a path through several enemies. A Flush calls forth the power of the Azure Dragon, Vermilion Bird, White Tiger, or Black Tortoise.
The four guardian beasts are the four regular suits. Rare Yellow Dragon variants bend their identity without turning the game into five-suit poker.

DOKKAEBI MASKS CHEAT THE RULES

Dokkaebi Masks are not ordinary stat gear. They can let four matching suits count as a Flush, make the lowest rank copy the highest, or cause the final scoring tile to echo again.
Arrange them freely between rooms. They trigger from left to right, so the same Masks in a different order can produce a different build.

THE HUSKS REMEMBER

Let a Husk escape and the run remembers what you took: the Soul Tile, the hand you were using, and the trick that made it work.
Later, that Husk returns as a Wraith carrying a distorted copy of your stolen power and an answer to your old build. Win the rematch and earn one guaranteed reward tied to what you stole: an upgrade for that tile, a cleansed curse, or a rare Knot.

BIG SCORES. REAL ACTION.

Power × Resonance lets a carefully built hand erupt into spectacular numbers. But raw score becomes a bounded Combat Grade instead of unchecked damage.
You still move, attack, dodge, counter, and extract by hand. A great build changes how you fight; it never fights in your place.

EVERY KING HAS A TABOO

Each boss announces one King's Taboo before the battle. The first Engraving may fall silent, your Masks may trigger in reverse, or a redraw may demand a price.
The rule is shown early enough to reorder your build or seek an answer on the road. It makes the fight harder, never impossible—and sharp action can still carry you through.

FIVE REGIONS. ABOUT 24 MINUTES.

Cross five continuous regions of a Joseon painted in folk-art ink, from grave-choked forest to drowned capital and the source beyond. Each region leans toward one guardian suit without locking you into it.
A full run is built around roughly 24 minutes of fights, elite hunts, Wraith ambushes, markets, strange encounters, shrines, and bosses.

EARLY ACCESS

FERAL PRINCE enters Early Access first. The core loop we want to build with you is simple to say and deep to master: fight, extract, forge, lock five—and feel that hand come alive in the next battle. The world and its possibilities will grow around that core.

FIND ALIEN is an online co-op stealth game for up to 4 players.

Rescue your captured fellow aliens — but don't let the people and agents around you discover who you really are.
Because you're an alien too. Copy the appearance of Earthlings to blend right in, slip past surveillance and traps, rescue your comrades, and escape together.

Copy an Earthling's appearance.

Walking around in your true alien form isn't a smart move. Copy the appearance of a nearby Earthling, disguise yourself as one of them, and stroll through the crowd like nothing's going on. But a disguise doesn't last forever. It drains over time, and the more eyes that land on you, the faster it goes. Run into the original owner of the appearance you copied, and it drains faster still.

Avoid surveillance and traps.

Even an ordinary-looking place isn't safe. In the mall, security guards are watching; inside B.A.R.D. facilities, it's the agents who track any suspicious movement. Slip past CCTV and lasers, cameras that seal off doors, electric floor panels that shock you, energy walls that strip away your disguise, and more. One slip-up can turn a quiet infiltration into chaos in an instant.

Get out before you're caught.

Linger in someone's line of sight with your cover blown and the detection gauge fills up — until a report goes through. Break line of sight before you're fully exposed. A step too slow, and capture agents are dispatched; once you're caught, you may be stuck inside a capsule, waiting for a teammate to come rescue you.

Get everyone out.

The moment you rescue the captured target alien, things get far more dangerous. Alarms blare, the agents tighten their guard, and now there's only one goal: everyone out. If a teammate's been caught, free them again — and make it out together, down to the last one.

Features

  • Up to 4-player co-op: Infiltrate with up to 3 friends.

  • Copy Earthling appearances: Copy the looks of nearby Earthlings to blend in and dodge surveillance.

  • Rescue captured teammates: Even a captured ally can be brought back.

  • A variety of infiltration tools: Use sleep bombs, smoke bombs, disguise extenders, self-escape devices, and more to draw attention away — though your allies might get caught in the blast too.

🏰 Three Epic Battlefields, Packed with Hidden Cats

Crowns fallen into golden treasuries, deep-sea wrecks brimming with gold, dwarven vaults fragrant with ale—in every 4K fantasy scene, sneaky kittens are hiding in plain sight.
Open your eyes wide and pick them out one by one across these legendary battlefields!

👑 Treasury Hall · Battle for the Crown

Golden-armored knights face thunder barbarians before the throne, Mjolnir scattering coins through the air. Crowns, gems, candelabras, picture frames—every spot may hide a cat.

⚓ Deep-Sea Wreck · Mermaids vs. Pirates

In the sunken pirate ship's cabin, mermaid archers battle a skeleton captain to the death. Treasure chests, shells, coral, seaweed—even the octopus's tentacles may hide a cat!

🍺 Vault Hall · Dwarves and Goblins Fight for the Ale Flagon

A white-bearded dwarf king clutches a golden flagon while a green goblin reaches out to snatch it. Gem piles, chains, scrolls, barrels—behind every gem, a cat is peeking at you.

🐱 Tons of Adorable Cats, Hiding in Every Corner

Each 4K HD scene hides 60 uniquely styled cute cats. From table legs to ceiling beams, from under cloaks to inside treasure chests—each strikes an unexpected pose, waiting for you to click and discover.

🎮 Simple Gameplay, Easy to Pick Up

Click, find, discover—three steps to complete a cat hunt. No time pressure, no combat controls, just the pure joy of that "Found it!" moment.

✨ Who Is This For?

· Players who love puzzles and discovery
· Anyone who enjoys epic fantasy themes and cute cats
· Casual players looking to rest their eyes amid a fast-paced world

Start your "finding cute cats in legendary battlefields" adventure today!

Finding Fairies is a cosy co-op fantasy investigation game where you and your friends use magical tools, teamwork, and deduction to discover which fairy is hiding nearby.

For generations, fairies lived quietly alongside humans, hidden deep within forests, gardens, ruins, and forgotten magical places. Most people believed they were only stories, glimpses of glowing lights in the trees or strange sounds carried on the wind.

But recently, fairy activity has begun to rise.

Magical traces are appearing across the land. Glowing petals have been found where no flowers grow. Strange footprints vanish moments after being discovered. Fairy dust reacts with unknown energy, enchanted orbs drift through the air, and mysterious sounds echo from places that should be silent.

To understand what is happening, a small group of fairy investigators has been formed.

That is where you come in.

Enter enchanted locations, search for evidence, and use your collection of magical investigation tools to identify the fairy before returning through the portal. Each fairy leaves behind a different combination of clues, so careful observation and teamwork are the key to solving each mystery.

Investigate Magical Activity

Explore beautiful fantasy environments and look for signs of nearby fairy activity. Evidence may be hidden in the world, appear only through certain tools, or reveal itself when the fairy interacts with the area.

Work Together or Play Solo

Play alone or with friends as you explore, investigate, and piece together the evidence.

Split up to cover more ground, stay together to compare clues, or assign each player a different tool. Every round challenges you to observe the environment, communicate clearly, and make the right final guess.

Identify the Fairy

Every fairy type has its own clue combination and behaviour. Once you have gathered enough evidence, use your journal to narrow down the possibilities and decide which fairy you believe is present.

When you are ready, submit your answer and return through the portal.

Choose correctly, and your investigation is a success.

Features

  • Cosy fantasy investigation gameplay

  • Solo and online co-op multiplayer

  • Magical tools for discovering hidden evidence

  • Different fairy types to identify

  • Beautiful enchanted environments

  • Replayable investigations with different evidence combinations

  • Team-based deduction and exploration

Findport never quite sleeps. Beneath the connected city runs another one, made of data, traffic and echoes — and you're one of the few who knows how to dive into it.

As captain of Unit 5, the Ministry division that investigates what no one else wants to touch, you've spent months pulling a thread that started with a corpse that still speaks. Four cases, seemingly unrelated. Four notes of a single phrase someone has been playing for you for a long time.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

— Investigate through dialogue: choose what to ask your team and anyone you question, and get the data you need before it's too late.

— Make decisions with no right answer, which the game will remember until the very end — literally.

— Dive into the Cybercosm: descend through the Channel and the Abyss, where information becomes territory.

— Earn the Margin's trust in its own currency, because down there your badge doesn't open doors — it closes them.

A GAME THAT REMEMBERS
Findport's endings aren't picked from a menu at the end of the run. They're earned through conduct. Everything you did — who you protected, what you kept quiet, who you trusted — accumulates, and an entity at the bottom of it all will read back exactly who you've been before it lets you decide what comes next.

THE WORLD
The Mesh, high and low. The Channel, that never stops flowing. The Abyss, where the city sinks what it wants to forget. And the Margin, where the rules are different — and worth more. A world painted in sepia-and-blue watercolor, where the police procedural and the philosophy are two sides of the same coin — for anyone who enjoyed Ghost in the Shell, or who's after the narrative density and the no-easy-way-out decisions of games like Disco Elysium.

WHAT YOU'LL FIND
· 6-8 hours in a first playthrough
· 4 endings, earned through conduct, not picked from a menu
· Spanish and English, both native languages of the game
· Original soundtrack
· A world written to be investigated, not just read

Spread your fire. Block your friends. Become King of the Isle.

Fire Isle is a turn-based strategy party game for 1–4 players inspired by the popular board game Blokus®. You play as a fire burning across an island. King Mongo launches pieces of himself, called Wisps, all around the island. Each turn, burn the tiles next to your fires to spread toward the latest Wisp. Burn a Wisp's tile first and it's yours. The fire with the most Wisps is crowned king.

If you've played the board game Blokus, you get the idea. If you haven't, here's the quick rundown: grow out from your own pieces, take the space your rivals need and leave them nowhere to go. Only here, nobody waits for a turn. Everyone races for the same tiles at the same time.

Every match is a free-for-all. Burn the cheap route your friend was counting on. Hide a trap on the tile they need next. Cut them off with a wall of Snow. Steal your friend's fire and sneak into the tiles they've been selfishly hoarding.

Your friend spent three turns spreading toward one? Snatch it with seconds left on the clock. Claim more of King Mongo's Wisps than your fiery brethren to be crowned his successor, the next King of Fire Isle.

Happy, Sad, Angry or Grumpy is just your look. Your class is how you fight.

Thief: steal an enemy fire beside yours to break their lines or shut them out.

Traveler: lob a fire over oceans, rivers, mountains, and enemy lines.

Storm Caster: summon an island-wide rainstorm that hurts your friends more than it hurts you.

Wisp Fiend: imagine not being able to just buy Wisps? Couldn't be you, L peasants.

Trapper: scatter exploding hidden traps around the map and watch your friends walk right into them at the best moments.

Warden: whoever said Sand, Stone, and Snow were hard to burn? For others, maybe, but not for you. Wall off rivals' paths with rough terrain at a moment's notice.

With 100+ cards to pick from, you can bend the rules, from cheaper fires to longer rainstorms and everything in between.

Unlike Cards, Items are one-time-use and where things get more aggressive. Slow down whoever's closest to winning with a Fire Extinguisher, jack up everyone else's prices with a Cold Front, make traps half-priced, and more.

Take advantage of what's available on every island; no two are exactly the same. Grass burns out fast, Forests and Swamps burn slower, Coal explodes in a burst of free fires, Ravines act as shortcuts, Rivers make crossing pricey, and Volcanoes launch your fire anywhere on the island.

Friends, Bots or Both

Host a lobby with your own rules, browse matches or send invites through Steam. No group tonight? Fill any empty seats with randoms or bots ranging in skill level from Journalist (it'd struggle to beat the tutorial if it tried) to Hard (it doesn't just target Wisps, it targets YOU).

After matches, Wisps you claimed can be spent at the Shop on cosmetics you and all your friends will see.

Pick a fire, pick a class, and pick some friends to duke it out with.

Fire Vow: Dark Fantasy is a single-player dark fantasy survival game built around card-based exploration, resource management, crafting, and combat.

Explore a cursed land where locations, resources, items, and enemies are represented as interactive cards. Move and combine cards to gather materials, prepare food, craft tools, equip weapons, and uncover new ways to survive.

Every action takes time and consumes valuable resources. Manage hunger, thirst, fatigue, injuries, weather conditions, and other status effects while deciding when to explore, rest, fight, or retreat.

Survive the journey, grow stronger, and ultimately defeat the Demon King.

Somewhere out there is an old brick-breaker cabinet that keeps more than high scores.

FIRST LIGHT is a story-rich arcade brick-breaker. Classic paddle-and-ball play, rebuilt around a century of one family's memories: one memory per level, told in their own voices, sealed against the Fog that takes unwitnessed things. Every wall you break is the Fog's work undone.

THE TELLING

  • 132 memories across four acts: a grandmother's river town, a father's patient hands, a boy's 1986 arcade summer… and the fourth, where the machine was built to keep them all
  • Fully voiced by five narrators, one memory before every level.
  • Four paintings hidden behind the four bosses, revealed brick by brick
  • An original 64-song soundtrack, nearly three hours of music, scored so each memory plays the song that agrees with it

THE GAME

  • Honest arcade brick-breaking: reflexes, angles, and nerve. Easy to start, hard to put down
  • A capsule economy that pays for risk: stack multipliers, bank speed, grow the light cannon — or catch the black pill on purpose
  • Four difficulties, from a gentle telling to one-life INSANE
  • Boss walls where the Fog itself fights back. Play calm; walls come down for patient hands
  • 33 achievements, three save campaigns, a high-score board with one name already on it: M-E-G

6–8 HOURS OF STORY, AND THE LIGHT AFTER

Beat it for the telling. Come back for AFTERGLOW: just the music, no stakes, endless. The achievement hunt. The board MEG left you to beat.

Combat in Firva is easy to grasp, but mastery demands timing, positioning, and the confidence to commit.

Master a system built around:

Fluid sword combos

Powerful charged attacks that interrupt enemies, even mini-bosses

Careful positioning under pressure

Reading attack patterns and exploiting recovery windows

Enemies coordinate their pressure around you. Those closest take priority in attacking, while others reposition and wait for their opportunity. Staying close to an enemy can keep them on the offensive, making movement and target selection essential to controlling the fight.

Your regular strikes deliver damage, while charged attacks let you break an opponent’s momentum and create an opening. Commit at the wrong moment, however, and a powerful interrupting strike can cut your own attack short.

Mini-bosses make every approach a calculated risk. Varied attacks and devastating area strikes punish careless aggression, but recovery windows give you a chance to close in and retaliate. Learn their rhythms, recognize their most dangerous moves, and turn each opening into an opportunity.

Victory demands a balance of aggression and patience: knowing when to apply pressure, when to reposition, and when to commit to a decisive blow.

Firva: Strings of Fate is a cinematic action-adventure built around exploration, platforming, puzzles, combat, and a dark fantasy story of revenge, loss, and fate.

Play as Firva, a warrior whose lifelong hunt for her parents’ killer leads her to the legendary Strings of Fate—mythical threads said to possess the power to bring the dead back to life. What begins as a journey of vengeance soon becomes a race against those who seek that power for themselves.

Journey through handcrafted environments, uncover hidden paths, survive dangerous encounters, solve environmental puzzles, and face powerful enemies as the story unfolds through cinematic sequences woven directly into the adventure.

Firva is a focused, story-rich journey inspired by the feeling of classic action-adventure games, where every place has a purpose, every encounter moves you forward, and the path may be yours to walk... but the destination has already been written.

Twenty years after the murder of her parents, Firva finally tracks down Ratiar the Butcher and takes the revenge she has spent her entire life waiting for.

But what she discovers on Ratiar’s body turns the end of her vengeance into the beginning of a far greater journey: one of the legendary Strings of Fate, a mythical thread said to hold the power to bring the dead back to life.

To awaken the String’s power, Firva needs the antlers of the Golden Deer—the very creature she grew up alongside, now living peacefully deep within the forest.

But when Firva returns home, she discovers that Rajoo is also searching for the String of Fate, and has already sent his hunters to claim it.

Now, Firva must reach the Golden Deer before they do and uncover a way to bring her parents back from the dead.

But Firva does not yet know what future the Weavers of Fate have spun for her. And when the day comes that she finally holds the true power of the Strings of Fate in her hands, will she still wish to bring her parents back from death... or will fate have something else in store for her?

A fixed, cinematic camera guides your perspective, emphasizing emotion, tension, and scale. From quiet,

reflective scenes to intense, breathtaking set pieces, the experience is designed to be seen, not just played.

Unable to speak, her story is told through action, animation, and the world around her. Her journey is not just one of survival, but of confronting past mistakes through the only language she knows: violence. 

Experience the world through Firva's eyes and ears, as a warrior trying to fix her past mistakes with only the method she knows; the Revenge

Become the Mute Warrior, Survive and outsmart the many enemies looking for your bow, and find out about the mysteries behind its origin.

From dense, haunting jungles to forgotten ruins and dreamlike landscapes, Ramirtana is filled with

hidden paths, environmental storytelling, and secrets waiting to be uncovered.

Firva: Strings of Fate is a character-driven story about:

  • Revenge and consequence

With dynamic narration and layered storytelling, each moment reveals new perspectives inviting you to

question what is real, and what is inevitable.

100 million fish in the sea. Catch them all.

Catch fish, earn money, learn skills, and catch even more. Fish Them All! is an incremental fishing game where your hauls get bigger and your fishing gets faster with every upgrade.

Your goal: 100 million fish in total. It sounds impossible at first, but every catch and every upgrade brings it steadily within reach.

Catch fish → Spend your earnings on skills → Catch even more!

The shutter clicks. The grid develops again.

Fission Mirror Grid is a turn-based roguelike that merges grid tactics, deckbuilding, and facing puzzles. A mirror-smith forged a cursed mirror to hold his love; an archaeologist unearthed it centuries later; a photographer trapped his soul inside a film camera—four travelers meet inside the Mirror Grid, a labyrinth of stolen memories, and fight by dragging negative-style skill cards across the board.

On a 14×6 battlefield you drag cards onto cells, reshape ranges with movement and card dyeing, and sequence Start, Instant, and End timings within the same turn. Fights aim for a tight 8-turn pace—every step and every facing change can flip the outcome.

14×6 mirror grid: drag to cast, move, preview

• Drag cards from the film-strip hand onto cells; each card shows range preview and sprocket-readable stats (damage, block, cost, heal)

• Facing drives forward shapes (single, line, cone, rectangle); other patterns include around-self, any cell, and self-only

• First 2 tiles moved each turn are free; further moves cost 1 Exposure each. Walking and dye-driven steps do not rotate facing—you need turn cards or dye settings for that

• Enemies telegraph intent; tiles can hold ongoing effects—right-click for intel

Card dyeing: turn and step before or after effects

Many cards add a facing turn or 1-tile move before or after they resolve, set via the dye ring (cool compass colors for facing, warm colors for movement). Builds are about dye, reposition, then cast: the same card hits different cells depending on how you dye it.

Start, Instant, End

All three timings are played during your action phase; resolution timing differs:

• Instant (amber) — resolves immediately on play: main damage, movement, control

• Start (teal) — played now, resolves at next turn start: setup buffs, auras, energy and shield refresh

• End (dusk purple) — played now, resolves at this turn end (before discard): delayed burst, counters, cleanup

A typical turn: lay Start cards for next turn, spend Instant cards for damage and positioning, then close with End. Energy-cap buffs usually kick in at next turn start to prevent one-turn spikes.

Exposure energy and hand flow

• Turn start: resolve queued Start effects, then face-up draw (about half your energy cap, rounded up; no blind pick) into the film hand; relics may add extra draws

• Action: play cards, move, turn—spend Exposure

• Turn end: resolve End effects, then clear the entire hand into the discard pile (nothing is kept)

• Energy cap shifts in battle (hard cap 3 to 15), changing draw count

Deckbuilding: 35–40 cards, about 100 cards and 119 relics

• Run decks target 35–40 cards; copy limits: 2 per common, rare, or epic, 1 legendary

• About 100 designed cards plus character-exclusive picks and 119 relics—damage, block, control, rule-benders

• Rewards, shops, and events reshape your deck each run

Branching mirror routes

Full game: 54 floors (3 acts × 18) with combats, elites, events, shops, and act bosses at floors 18, 36, and 54. Spend Exposure Shards and pick routes—trade-offs between path, resources, and deck plan, not just bigger numbers.

Four camera travelers

All four are selectable from the start, each with a unique starter relic, exclusive cards, and canister color:

• Shutter Prisoner (hero, compact 35mm) — soul sealed in a camera. Film-roll loop: spend full rolls to release sealed memories, then empty rolls; Memory Imprint Shop sells deck cards on the left wall and film developing plus relics on the right

• Mirror Smith (brass box camera) — the mirror's ancient maker. Blanks, block, mirror copy

• Archaeologist (half-frame silver) — modern scholar pulled into the grid. Rubbings, parsing, rewind—control and mechanic breaks

• Mirror Lord (heroine, warped mirror body) — the mirror's host. Reflection, memory devour, spatial fracture

Each traveler has a themed shop. Cross-era encounters, character-specific events, and mirror hazard zones weave one narrative line.

Light meta: expand pools, not stats

Meta progression unlocks card and relic reward pools and a gallery—no permanent attack or HP inflation. Deeper runs and total wins widen what you can roll; each run still starts from a character kit and fresh choices inside the grid.

Film-strip UI

Negative-style cards, sprocket stat chips, canister deck and discard counts, horizontal film hand—battle info you can read at a glance. Click the canister to browse deck and discard piles (read-only).

Demo

The demo is a full Chapter 1 (18 floors): all four characters available; ends after the floor-18 act boss. The full game continues through Chapters 2–3 to the summit finale and expanded character storylines. Wishlist and feedback welcome.

For you if…

• You want roguelike deckbuilders with real grid positioning, facing, and range geometry

• You enjoy sequencing dye, movement, and timing layers under pressure

• You like darkroom film aesthetics, looping narrative, and 8-turn tactical fights

• You want four distinct protagonists, unique kits, and a replayable branching map

You play as Alan, a delivery courier with a 4.7 rating and two days left to pay off his debt.
Today, Almaty is shrouded in a strange fog that smells of death — a fog that, according to rumor, dissolves the boundary between the living and the dead.
What should be a routine shift turns into a fight for survival: to clear his debt and earn those precious five stars, Alan must complete special orders while the city is swallowed by something dark and unexplainable.
Will you help the courier — or turn this shift into the worst of his life?

Meet terrifying characters inspired by Turkic mythology and the legends of the city of Almaty. Don't let them win you over to their side.

Almaty has changed, even though it looks the same. A sinister entity has taken hold of it from within. Something otherworldly hides behind its familiar facade. Demolished landmarks have been restored.

Shape the course of history with your choices. You'll not only have to make decisions but also demonstrate mastery of your profession.

Key Features:

  • Two storylines

  • Black-and-white pixel art aesthetic

  • Real-world locations and creatures inspired by Kazakh folklore

You start with nothing but yourself.

One hero on an empty, forgotten field, and the remains of an old, shattered empire. The kingdom fell. Take it back one flag at a time!

The loop

Build an army, kill the bad guys, program your units battle logic with Gambits, and push flag by flag into depths that never stop scaling. Every run ends one way: you spend what you earned and go again, stronger.

Deploy

Field nine unit classes, each with its own skill pool, a subclass to evolve into, and Regalia gear you craft, roll and star. Your roster carries between runs, levels in the barracks, and yes, you can name them.

Push

Auto-battle across zones that scale as you advance, or engage hands on with your hero. Capture flags, slay bosses, and slay the Maw. Descend through fracture depths that each change the rules: unwoven portals, awakened bosses, scars that follow you between zones. Ten are named today, twenty are planned, and the endless Tower waits past all of them.

Prestige

Retreat is progress, and death is a lesson learned. Bank your loot, level the barracks, unlock three hero classes, the Warlord, the Ranger and the Mage, each with a full skill pool and no hard level cap, and stack relics and artifacts that change how the next run plays.

Defend

Participate in King of the Hill and other players will fight your army while you sleep. Climb the seasonal ladder, review every attack in the match log, and take your revenge!

  • Gambits: program unit behavior with no coding required. Kite at 50 pixels, focus the backline, retreat at 25% HP.

  • Three heroes, one command: Warlord, Ranger, and Mage, each with a full skill pool.

  • Regalia crafting: roll it, enhance it, star it, equip it to gear out your units.

  • The Tower: an endless procedural gauntlet to test your mettle.

  • Fully localized in English, 日本語, 한국어, and 简体中文.

Small kitchen. Big care.

Welcome to Flame, Cats & Kitchen, a cozy cooking game set in a colorful paper kitchen. Cat guests arrive with their own meal requests, and your job is to turn a handful of ingredients into something they'll enjoy.

Draw it. Cut it. Cook it.

Pick an ingredient base and turn it into your own paper creation. Draw, color, and cut out its shape with scissors. Add a taste accent with special flavor crayons, then take your creation straight to the stove. Save your favorite designs as reusable templates so your next meal can include another helping.

Find the right flavor

Mix ingredients in a pan or pot, stir to reveal their flavors, and experiment with combinations. Keep the heat gentle, or use the pan to give your ingredients a browned finish. Watch the pan's heat: even a cozy kitchen can have a burnt dinner.

A good meal for every cat

Listen to each guest's request and find a combination that suits them. A firefighter looking for something hot and spicy may need a very different dish from a gardener who wants a milder meal. Serve your creation, see their reaction, and earn Karma for getting it right.

Crayon textures, cardboard edges, warm lighting, and a kitchen full of little details make every visit feel like stepping into a colorful paper world.
